source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW1 campus in Carrollton, Texas publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space, and it is one of only 19 Texas facilities that publish a megawatt figure at all.

The 45 MW is the operator's own number, not an estimate. The spec page does not publish an address, a postal code, or a tenant list, so nothing here identifies who runs inside the building. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualify the campus to host payment card data, protected health data, federal information systems, and audited financial controls, and TIA-942 speaks to the physical topology of the facility. None of them name a customer.

The published spec does not state a rack count, a rack density, or a cooling method, so the accelerator count is not derivable from this data. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 45 MW of IT load is roughly 1,125 racks. At 130 kW per rack, a plausible figure for a dense liquid-cooled deployment, the same 45 MW is about 346 racks. Both figures rest on an assumption the operator did not make.

Texas is the largest state on the map by facility count, with 137 mapped facilities, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, and DFW1's 45 MW ranks third among them. The gap between 137 mapped and 19 publishing is the real constraint on any count: most of the state's capacity is invisible to it, and this campus is one of the few that lets itself be counted.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
